    *   Malthus (1798, *An Essay on the Principle of Population*) argued that population grows geometrically (exponentially) while food production grows arithmetically (linearly).
    *   He predicted a "positive check" on population (famine, war, disease) to keep numbers in check.
    *   Modern demography/economics refutes Malthus because population *has* followed a pattern where food production can keep up or even exceed population growth (Green Revolution, etc.).

3.  **Evaluate Options:**
    *   A. "human population grew in an arithmetic manner, not an exponential one": Incorrect. Population growth has been exponential/geometric, matching Malthus's prediction on that specific variable.
    *   B. "the J-curve of population always exceeds the J-curve of food production": Incorrect. If this were true, Malthus would have been right regarding catastrophe (starvation). Food production has largely caught up due to technology.
    *   C. "soil erosion has limited food production capabilities...": This actually makes the catastrophe more likely or explains local failures, not why the general catastrophe hasn't occurred.
    *   D. "changes occurred in the quantity and quality of food consumption in First-World countries": While consumption patterns change, this doesn't explain the global capacity to feed the population.
    *   E. "the invention of agricultural technology boosted the value of food production": Correct. The Green Revolution, synthetic fertilizers, mechanization, and biotechnology have allowed food production to grow geometrically/exponentially, outpacing population growth and averting the Malthusian disaster.
